Rashi on Menachot 3b:2:1.hebrew: מנחה לשם מנחה - מחבת לשם מרחשת, עלו:
Rashi on Menachot 3b:2:1.english: A meal offering for the sake of a meal offering - [Such as a] pan [meal offering sacrificed] for the sake of a deep pan [meal offering; in this case,] they fulfill [the owner's obligation].

Rashi on Menachot 3b:4:1.english: But doesn't the tanna say: "Its actions prove what it is"? - Therefore, a meal offering [offered] for the sake of a slaughtered offering should also be valid.

Rashi on Menachot 3b:4:2.hebrew: ה"ק - אע"פ שאין המנחות דומות לזבחים, דאע"ג דהקומץ מחבת לשם מרחשת מחשבה דלא מינכרא שיהיה כן היא, אלא ודאי ניכר שאינו כן, דהא מעשיה מוכיחים, איכא למימר דתיפסל, דודאי סבירא לן מחשבה הגלויה לכל שהוא מכזב כל שכן שהיא פסולה — אפילו הכי עלו, דכתיב: "זאת תורת המנחה". הא "לא מינכרא" לא דמי לההוא דלעיל. רבא ורב אשי סבירא להו דמחשבה הגלויה לכל שהוא מכזב כל שכן שפוסלת, והכי מתרצי לקמן: אדרבה, מחשבה דמינכרא שהיא שקר פסל רחמנא, שמא יאמרו מותר לשנות בקרבנות:
Rashi on Menachot 3b:4:2.english: This is what he is saying - Even though meal offerings are not similar to slaughtered offerings, for even though one who removes a handful from a pan [meal offering] for the sake of a deep-pan [meal offering] has an intention that is not recognizable as being so, but rather it is certainly recognizable that it is not so, since its preparation proves [it], and one might say that it should be disqualified, for we certainly hold that an intention where it is obvious to all that he is lying is all the more so disqualified — even so, they fulfilled [the owner's obligation], as it is written: "This is the law of the meal offering." This [usage of] "not recognizable" is not similar to that above. Rava and Rav Ashi hold that an intention where it is obvious to all that he is lying is all the more so disqualifying, and this is how they explain later: "On the contrary, the Merciful One disqualified an intention that is recognizably false, lest they say: It is permitted to alter sacrificial offerings."

Rashi on Menachot 3b:5:1.hebrew: ומאי אבל בזבחים אינו כן - דמשמע התם דין הוא דלא עלו משום דשחיטה אחת לכולן, הא כל שכן דדין הוא דעלו במחשבה דלא מינכר שהוא שקר היא:
Rashi on Menachot 3b:5:1.english: And what is: "But with regard to slaughtered offerings it is not so" - For it implies that there [with regard to slaughtered offerings], it stands to reason that they do not fulfill [the owner's obligation] because there is one manner of slaughter for all of them; whereas all the more so it stands to reason that they should fulfill [the owner's obligation], in [the case of] an intention where it is not recognizable that it is a lie.

Rashi on Menachot 3b:6:1.hebrew: דהא שחיטה אחת לכולן - ואיכא למימר דתעלה לשם חובה, דהא ליכא למיגזר שמא יאמרו מותר לשנות בזבחים; אפילו הכי לא עלו, דזאת תורת המנחה וזבח לא כתיב, דליהוי משמע תורה אחת לכל המנחות, ותורה אחת לכל הזבחים:
Rashi on Menachot 3b:6:1.english: For there is one slaughter for all of them - And one could say that it should fulfill [the owner's] obligation, for there is no [reason] to decree lest [people] say: "It is permitted to change [the designation of] slaughtered offerings"; [yet] even so, they do not fulfill [the obligation], as "This is the law of the meal offering and the slaughtered offering" is not written, which would mean: one law for all meal offerings and one law for all slaughtered offerings.

Tosafot on Menachot 3b:2:1.hebrew: כאן בקומץ מנחה לשם זבח - בחנם נקט רבא ענין זה, דלא איירי ביה בשום דוכתא; דתירוץ זה עצמו, שמחלק משום דכתיב זאת תורת המנחה, היה יכול לתרץ כמו שתירץ רבה: כאן בשינוי קודש, כאן בשינוי בעלים; בשינוי קודש כשר, משום דתורה אחת לכל המנחות. ושמא לפיכך שינה לשונו של רבה, דהוה משמע, אם היה אומר כאן בשינוי קודש, דשינוי קודש כשר אפי' במנחה לשם זבח. ועוד יש לומר, דדייק לישנא דברייתא, דמשמע ליה קמצה שלא לשמה פסולה בשינוי קודש. ולקמן, דקאמר כולהו כרבה לא אמרי, ולא מפרש טעמא זה – ניחא לו למימר טעם השוה לכל האמוראים:
Tosafot on Menachot 3b:2:1.english: Here, where one removes a handful from a meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering - Rava introduced this case unnecessarily, as it is not discussed anywhere [else]; for with this very resolution—which distinguishes [between cases] because it is written, "This is the law of the meal offering" (Leviticus 6:7)—he could have resolved [the contradiction] just as Rabba resolved: Here [it refers to] a change of sanctity, [and] there [it refers to] a change of ownership; in [a case of] a change of sanctity it is valid, because [there is] "one law for all meal offerings." And perhaps he altered Rabba's wording for this reason: for it would have implied, had he said "here [it refers to] a change of sanctity," that a change of sanctity is valid even in [the case of] a meal offering [sacrificed] for the sake of a slaughtered offering. And furthermore, one can say that he was precise regarding the wording of the baraita, as it implied to him that [when it states] "if one removed a handful from it not for its own sake it is disqualified," [it refers specifically to] a change of sanctity. And below, where it says: "All of them did not state [their resolutions] in accordance with Rabba," and does not explain this reason [i.e., that "not for its own sake" denotes a change of sanctity]—it was preferable for it [the Gemara] to state a reason that applies equally to all the Amoraim.

Tosafot on Menachot 3b:4:1.hebrew: אע"ג דמחשבה דלא מינכרא היא ותיפסל - הרבה יש לתמוה, למה שינה לשונו מלישנא דלעיל בריש שמעתא, דמה שקורא לעיל מינכרא קורא הכא לא מינכרא, וחד פירושא לתרוייהו: דמינכרא היינו שניכר שמחשבתו שקר, ולא מינכרא דהכא היינו דאין ניכר שיהא כמו שהוא מחשב, אלא אדרבה ניכר שאינו כמו שהוא מחשב. ושמא שינה הלשון לפי שהוא כמו נתינת טעם דתיפסל, לפיכך ניחא ליה למינקט הכא ולעיל על פסול לשון לא מינכרא. ובסוף שמעתא, דקאמר כולהו כרבה לא אמרי, אדרבה מחשבה דמינכרא פסל רחמנא, משום דקאי ארבה, נקט לשון מינכרא על פסול:
Tosafot on Menachot 3b:4:1.english: Even though it is an intention that is not recognizable, and it should be disqualified - There is much reason to wonder: Why did [the Gemara] change its phrasing from the phrasing earlier at the beginning of the sugya? For that which it calls earlier "recognizable" (minkara), it calls here "not recognizable" (lo minkara), even though both have one [and the same] meaning: namely, that "recognizable" means that it is recognizable that his intention is false, while "not recognizable" here means that it is not recognizable that [the offering] is as he intends, but rather on the contrary, it is recognizable that it is not as he intends. And perhaps [the Gemara] changed the wording because it is like providing a reason why it should be disqualified; therefore, it was convenient for it to employ, both here and earlier, the term "not recognizable" for disqualification. And at the end of the sugya, where it states: "All of them do not say like Rabba; on the contrary, the Merciful One disqualified recognizable intention" — because it is addressing Rabba, it employed the term "recognizable" for disqualification.
